## 1.
Write a program which prints all factors of the number $N$.
The code which prints the factors should be placed inside a function.
Print an additional message to the console if $N$ is a prime number.

## 2.
Modify the program in such a way that it prints all prime numbers inside the range $\{1,\ldots,\mathrm{M}\}$.
Modify the function which prints factors so that it only returns information whether a number is prime or not.

## 3.
Write a program to see how you can use pointers and arrays:

- declare an integer variable `d`,
- initialize `d` with `10`,
- declare an integer pointer `p`,
- initialize pointer `p` with the address of the variable `d` (`p` points to `d`),
- print the value of `d` and the value which is pointed to by `p` (use operator `*`),
- change the value of `d` to `20`,
- print the value of `d` and the value which is pointed to by `p`,
- change the value pointed to by `p`,
- print the value of `d` and the value which is pointed to by `p`,
- print the address of `d` and the value of the pointer `p` (remember that the pointer stores the address, use the `printf` function, e.g.: `printf("%p", &d);`)
- declare an array `tab` of integers with two elements (`int tab[2];`)
- initialize elements of the array with: `333` and `444`,
- assign to the pointer `p` the address of the array `tab`,
- fill the following table:

| Address of variable | Name of the variable | Value of the variable |
|---------------------|----------------------|-----------------------|
|        %p           |          d           |          %d           |
|        %p           |          p           |          %p           |
|        %p           |          p[0]        |          %d           |
|        %p           |          t           |          %p           |
|        %p           |          t[0]        |          %d           |
|        %p           |          t[1]        |          %d           |
- find the distance (in bytes) between the addresses of the first and the second elements of the table `tab`
